title: Night Wings: The True Story of a Little Brown Bat
summary: In this true story, a tiny little brown bat wakes at dusk, flies on wings that are really hands, finds moths in the dark with echoes, and snuggles into a quiet cave to hibernate for the winter.
character: the little brown bat, ONE small realistic little brown bat with sleek short warm cocoa-brown fur, a slightly paler tan belly, large pointed oval dark brown ears, a pointed dark brown snout, tiny shiny black eyes and thin dark brown leathery wings with long slender finger bones

cover.text: Night Wings: The True Story of a Little Brown Bat.

pages.spokenText: In an old barn, a tiny brown bat hangs upside down. She weighs about as much as three pennies!
Special cords in her feet lock her toes tight, so hanging is easy. At sunset, she wakes up.
Bats sleep about twenty hours a day! She yawns, stretches, and combs her fur clean like a cat.
Bats are not birds. They are mammals with fur, and baby bats, called pups, drink their mother's milk.
She lets go, drops into the air, and flies! Bats are the only mammals that can truly fly.
Her wings are really her hands, with long finger bones. Bats' scientific name even means hand-wing!
Other little brown bats zig and zag out of the barn too. When you go to bed, it's their breakfast time!
How does she find bugs in the dark? She calls out squeaks too high for us to hear.
The squeaks bounce off a moth as echoes, which tell her where it is. This is called echolocation!
She scoops up the moth with her wing. She can catch hundreds of bugs in one hour!
Down at the pond, she skims the still water and takes a sip while she flies.
Eating bugs helps farmers and means fewer mosquito bites! Far away, fruit bats spread seeds and pollen for plants.
All night she eats and rests. When the sky turns pink at dawn, she flies home to the barn.
As autumn nights grow cold, she eats and eats. Her extra fat is like a packed lunch for winter.
One chilly night, she flies to a big, quiet cave in the hills, where many bats gather.
Inside the cave it is dark and damp, not freezing and not warm, but just right.
She hooks her toes on the rock, wraps her wings like a blanket, and begins to hibernate.
Her body cools and her racing heart slows way, way down. She will sleep almost all winter.
Outside, snow falls softly over the hills. Inside, the little brown bat dreams, upside down and cozy.
In spring, she will fly into the evening sky again. But for now, goodnight, little bat.

end.text: The end. Goodnight, little bat, and sweet dreams!
